newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Lifeless trading in the Spanish debt market ended with slightly higher prices on Wednesday, while dealers held back ahead of January CPI, out tomorrow.
"We kept our arms crossed all day, as everybody was already positioned for tomorrow's CPI and Friday's repo," said a dealer with a U.S. house in Madrid.

He added that even if inflation cames out as in a perceived worst-case scenario -- at 0.5 percent month-on-month and 3.1 percent year-on-year -- "there is still the possibility that the Bank of Spain will cut rates".
A Reuter poll showed a consensus opinion for the CPI to rise 0.4 percent from December, to 3.0 percent on the year.
But not all dealers had such strong expectations of a cut by the Bank of Spain.
"The peseta is stronger now, but I expect a more cautious approach by the Bank of Spain this year," an economist said.
Spain's central bank has pushed its key money rate to the current 6.0 percent from nine percent at the beginning of 1996.
"The Bank of Spain knows how lagged the effect of monetary policy is -- and they are already looking at 1998 perspectives, which are worse than this year's," he said.
